column1: # Example lines of a made-up mod, "examplemod", for the Lonapse API (docs/API.md).
# Put a file like this in GameData/<YourMod>/Lonapse/ and Lonapse reads it at the first flight scene.
# The format is that of GameData/Lonapse/Phrases/Runtime (explained at the top of reports.tsv). For mod events:
#   on=yourmod.event   the event of a chat (an event chat: the kerbal who did it says line 1) or of an event line
#   kind event         a Mission Control line about the event. A reply with to= its id lets the kerbal answer.
#   kind meta          the settings of an event: cooldown=<seconds> (default 120), priority=low|normal|high,
#   {x_name}           your own values, sent with the event. A number becomes Spanish words in the voice and digits
#                      in the subtitle, a name is said as it is. Every version uses the same slots in both languages.
# Ids start with rt_ and must be unique over all files: start them with rt_<yourmod>_ (chats rt_chat_<yourmod>_...).

column4: spanish
column5: english

column1: # meta rows: the settings of each event (all optional).
# examplemod.repair_done, sent with the kerbal who did it and x_part, the part with its article.

column4: {other}, ya está arreglado: {x_part}. | {other}, reparación terminada.
column5: {other}, it's fixed: {x_part}. | {other}, repair done.

column4: ¿Y por qué sobra un tornillo? | Buen trabajo. ¿Has usado cinta?
column5: Then why is there a screw left over? | Good work. Did you use tape?

column4: Es de repuesto. | Mucha. Mucha cinta.
column5: It's a spare. | Lots. Lots of tape.

column1: # One line, for a kerbal alone.

column4: Reparación terminada. Me ha sobrado un tornillo. | Arreglado. Creo. Bueno, ya no hace ruido.
column5: Repair done. I have a screw left over. | Fixed. I think. Well, it stopped making noise.

column1: # Mission Control about it, and the kerbal's answer.

column4: {kerbal}, vemos la reparación en los datos. Buen trabajo. | Reparación recibida. Ya no parpadea nada en la pantalla.
column5: {kerbal}, we see the repair in the data. Good work. | Repair confirmed. Nothing is blinking on the screen anymore.

column4: Gracias. No toquéis nada. | De nada. Sobró un tornillo, por cierto.
column5: Thanks. Don't touch anything. | You're welcome. One screw left over, by the way.

column1: # examplemod.supplies_low, sent with x_days, the days of supplies left. A check on x_days keeps the plural right.

column4: {other}, quedan provisiones para {x_days} días. | {other}, la despensa dice {x_days} días.
column5: {other}, we have supplies for {x_days} days. | {other}, the pantry says {x_days} days.

column4: Entonces nada de segundas raciones. | Vale. Escondo mis galletas.
column5: Then no second helpings. | Okay. I'm hiding my cookies.

column4: Lo apunto en la lista. | Me parece bien.
column5: I'll put it on the list. | Sounds fair.

column4: Os quedan provisiones para {x_days} días. Planead la vuelta. | Según los datos, {x_days} días de provisiones. Comed despacio.
column5: You have supplies for {x_days} days. Plan the trip home. | The data says {x_days} days of supplies. Eat slowly.

column4: Solo queda comida para un día. Volved pronto.
column5: Only one day of food left. Come home soon.

column1: # examplemod.experiment_done, sent with x_experiment as "spanish|english". who=mc: only Mission Control.

column4: Experimento de {x_experiment} terminado. Los científicos ya miran los datos. | Recibido: {x_experiment}, completo. Buen trabajo, {kerbal}.
column5: The {x_experiment} experiment is done. The scientists are looking at the data. | Copy: {x_experiment}, complete. Good work, {kerbal}.

column4: Ha sido fácil. Casi. | Gracias. El manual ayudó mucho.
column5: That was easy. Almost. | Thanks. The manual helped a lot.

column1: # An experiment of your own that runs through the KSP science system (a ModuleScienceExperiment with experimentID
# exampleSoil). Lonapse sees it like a stock experiment, so do not call Trigger for it. The experiment row gives {exp}
# its words and names its topic. Science lines and event chats with on=examplemod.soil only play for it.

column4: análisis del suelo
column5: soil analysis

column4: Recibimos el {exp}. Mucha tierra, pocas sorpresas. | Ya tenemos el {exp}. Los geólogos están contentos.
column5: We have the {exp}. Lots of dirt, few surprises. | The {exp} is in. The geologists are happy.

column4: {other}, el {exp} está listo. Es tierra.
column5: {other}, the {exp} is done. It's dirt.

column4: ¿Solo tierra? | ¿Tierra buena, al menos?
column5: Just dirt? | Good dirt, at least?

column4: Tierra muy científica.
column5: Very scientific dirt.

column4: Ya tengo el {exp}. Es tierra, sobre todo.
column5: I have the {exp}. It's mostly dirt.

column1: # A Breaking Ground part of your own (a ModuleGroundSciencePart, part name exampleDrillRig). Lonapse sees the deploy
# itself. The device row gives {device} its words and names its topic. Chats with on=deploy play for it too.

column4: el taladro
column5: the drill rig

column4: {other}, {device} ya está montado.
column5: {other}, {device} is set up.

column4: ¿Y si encuentra agua? | ¿Hace mucho ruido?
column5: What if it finds water? | Is it loud?

column4: Entonces somos ricos. | Solo un poco.
column5: Then we're rich. | Only a little.

column4: Llegan datos: {device} funciona.
column5: Data is coming in: {device} works.

column1: # A contract type of your own (the class name of your Contract, ExampleSalvageContract). The contract row gives

column5: the salvage job

column4: Listo: {contract}. Os pagan {funds} fondos.
column5: Done: {contract}. It pays {funds} funds.

column4: Hemos perdido {contract}. Otra vez será.
column5: We lost {contract}. Maybe next time.

column4: Listo: {contract}. Buen trabajo.
column5: Done: {contract}. Good work.
